body:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Jets
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn delivered some troubling news on Tuesday, as first-round pick tight end Kenyon Sadiq is going to miss some time after "having a little setback." There's not an exact timetable for his return, although Glenn doesn't think Sadiq will miss the season opener. The rookie had offseason hernia surgery. 
The No. 16 overall pick was the top tight end in his past draft, setting career highs with 51 catches for 560 yards and eight touchdowns for the Oregon Ducks last season. No FBS tight end caught more touchdowns than Sadiq. He was expected to make an immediate impact on this Jets offense, but New York does have another capable tight end in Mason Taylor. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ers
McCaffrey missed Monday's practice with what the team called "tightness," which obviously doesn't provide much in the way of information. CMC is coming off a season during which he led the NFL with 413 touches, then recorded 37 more in two playoff games. He has a history of breaking down following seasons with huge workloads, so any missed practice time is obviously worth monitoring.
Pearsall is expected to undergo season-ending surgery on his ongoing PCL injury that has been an issue since last season. Niners general manager John Lynch said that Pearsall is expected to make a full recovery. 
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return. 
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice. 
Bosa missed Saturday's practice with "soreness," and on Tuesday 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the star pass rusher is considered week to week due to tendinitis in his surgically repaired knee.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City Chiefs
Allen, who had been enjoying a strong start to his first NFL camp, was carted off the field on Saturday after colliding with Kaiir Elam on a special teams drill. ESPN later reported that test conducted on Allen revealed a shin bruise. Nothing was torn or broke, so he appears to have dodged a bullet. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buffalo Bills
During Saturday's practice, Johnson went down and was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was aided off the field. He was also seen clutching the area around his Achilles. Despite being carted to the locker room, ESPN reports that Gardner-Johnson merely suffered a lower calf strain, so he avoided any serious injury.Johnson, 28, was enjoying a solid start to training camp. A seven-year veteran, Johnson's NFL accolades includes a Super Bowl win with the Eagles and leading the NFL in interceptions back in 2022. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Atlanta Falcons 
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush. Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
Atlanta brought its Aug. 4 practice to a close after Walker went down with a leg injury. It is feared to be a torn ACL for the second-year edge rusher. His Falcons teammates took knees and surrounded him while trainers evaluated him, and he was then carted off the field. Walker sustained the injury in an 11-on-11 two-minute drill at the Falcons' non-padded practice.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Carolina Panthers
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp. Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited. Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic. The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
Former first-round pick Xavier Legette reportedly went down hard on his back and head while attempting to make a catch during drills on Tuesday. After remaining on the turf for some time, the wideout was helped up and carted off the field, per WCNC. While it doesn't appear Legette suffered a serious, season-ending injury, it was another scare for a team that has already suffered too many losses in training camp. Legette is still looking to live up to his No. 32 overall pick billing. In 15 games played last year, he caught 35 passes for 363 yards and three touchdowns. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New Orleans Saints
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season. 
Jordan is dealing with a hamstring injury that head coach Kellen Moore said could go into the regular season. Moore added "we'll see" as the Saints are continuing to evaluate the issue. New Orleans has already lost one defensive lineman for the season and can scarcely afford to lose another contributor up front.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cincinnati Bengals
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled. Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN, Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Detroit Lions
McNeill left Friday's practice with a neck injury suffered in a pile-up during 11-on-11 drills, according to the Detroit Free Press. The Lions are already shorthanded in the secondary and can scarcely use an injury up front. McNeil wasn't himself last season after returning from a torn ACL and it's not a great sign to see him banged up early in camp this year.
The Lions signed former Panthers center Cade Mays to a three-year deal worth $25 million this offseason to replace Graham Glasgow. However, Mays suffered a wrist injury that will force him to miss a "significant period of time," per head coach Dan Campbell. Mays will return at some point this year, "but it will be down the road."
Campbell told reporters that new running back Isiah Pacheco suffered an MCL sprain in practice, but that he is expected to be ready for the season opener vs. New Orleans.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New England Patriots
Brown told NFL Media that he dislocated his thumb at a Patriots practice. Brown returned to practice and caught several passes. "Thumb out of place," he said. "You keep going." This is certainly going to be an important injury to monitor. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chicago Bears
Bryant suffered a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture during practice. While his initial recovery timeline of eight to 10 weeks would have put him on track to return by the season's midpoint, the cornerback could now miss the entire regular season. Bryant underwent surgery on the injured knee and will now miss four to six months, coach Ben Johnson announced. The Bears are hopeful he will be available for the playoffs should they clinch a berth.It's a brutal blow for a Bears secondary that was already one of the thinner units on the team. It's also rough for Bryant, who signed a big free agent deal with Chicago this offseason.
CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports that Bears wideout Luther Burden III suffered a groin injury after a one-on-one rep vs. Tyrique Stevenson in the red zone, and is expected to miss about a month. The Bears hope he can return for the Sept. 13 season opener against Carolina. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arizona Cardinals
Benson experienced discomfort and flaring in his surgically-repaired knee, according to head coach Mike LaFleur. He was feeling better on Monday August 3, which LaFleur said was good news, and added that it's not likely to be a multi-week issue. Still, it's never a good sign when a player who had surgery experiences "discomfort" in the body part that was repaired. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baltimore Ravens
Wiggins was carted off the field during the Ravens' Aug. 11 practice after he went down in the end zone while covering rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane in one-on-one drills. Wiggins appeared to have some sort of leg or knee injury, per reporters on the scene. The Ravens are relatively thin at cornerback behind Wiggins, so this is a potentially major injury for a defense looking to bounce back under first-year head coach Jesse Minter, who offered an update: "I don't have a ton of information yet. ... I think there's optimism."  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Washington Commanders
Tunsil is out indefinitely after suffering torn triceps. The left tackle will miss at least a good amount of the regular season and will likely need surgery, per NFL Network.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indianapolis Colts
Pierce has yet to practice as he recovers from ankle surgery he underwent this offseason. He was placed on the team's PUP list ahead of training camp. General manager Chris Ballard clarified that Pierce did not receive a second platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection in his ankle, as had previously been reported, and stated that he anticipates Pierce will be ready for Week 1.
Ward did not travel with the Colts for their joint practice with the Patriots. General manager Chris Ballard said Ward dealt with some pain after Sunday's practice, so he stayed in Indianapolis to rehab.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay Packers 
Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Tuesday that Jacobs will be out for "at least a week" as he continues to deal with a groin injury. The injury initially sidelined Jacobs during last Thursday's practice. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia Eagles 
Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Tuesday that it will be "another couple of weeks at least" until Greenard will be able to resume football activities. Greenard hasn't practice since he sustained a pectoral strain while lifting weights before the start of training camp.

title: Vikings name Kyler Murray starting QB over J.J. McCarthy - CBS Sports
description: The Vikings' QB battle has ended prior to the beginning of the preseason
body:
The Vikings' QB battle has ended prior to the beginning of the preseason
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The quarterback battle in Minnesota has come to a swift conclusion, as the Vikings have named Kyler Murray their new starter over former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy. Head coach Kevin O'Connell informed the team of his decision on Tuesday. This battle was expected to last into the preseason, but O'Connell called the contest four days before the Vikings are scheduled to take the field against the New York Giants. As for the status of McCarthy, O'Connell said he is slotted in as the backup and "he's ready to go." "There's moments in time where you know there's comfort from Kyler in the scheme,'' O'Connell said. "He had some really high completion days where he was able to show some really, really good understanding of just putting the ball in play, playing with great timing, rhythm. You guys have seen him be explosive when there's opportunities there, but you've also seen him check the ball down and put the ball in play and get us from a first-and-10 to a second-and-3. And then, as you continued to look at the body of work through those 10 days, what jumped out is what could be."Murray will be the Vikings' fourth different Week 1 starting quarterback over the last four years. He was always viewed as the favorite to win this job over McCarthy, who became the only first-round pick since 1970 to finish last in the NFL in completion percentage and TD-INT ratio in his first season. While Minnesota did rally to finish with a 9-8 record last year, the Vikings still missed the playoffs thanks to an underperforming offense.Despite the demotion, the Vikings still believe McCarthy has a bright future ahead.
"He's still a guy that's only played 10 games,'' O'Connell said. "He's shown improvement off of last year. Even in this training camp with the work he's put in and his comfort level, just growing a little bit day in and day out. Very excited to continue to get to work with him every single day, coach him. "As he knows, he's holding the pen on his story and we're gonna support him and try to just help him continue to improve at the most difficult position in sports. He's gotta also understand, this isn't just a long-term mindset, which we want to have always for a player of his caliber and a young player like him, but it could be an immediate response needed. J.J.'s the kind of guy that'll be ready to rock and roll, I know that."Murray was released by the Arizona Cardinals this offseason following seven years with the franchise. The former No. 1 overall pick won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2019, made two Pro Bowls, and took Arizona to the postseason once, but his play dipped in recent years. Murray has missed 30 out of a possible 68 games over the last five seasons, and his last winning season came back in 2021. In all, Murray went 38-48-1 during his time with the Cardinals. Still, it's possible Murray is rejuvenated by this change of scenery. In Minnesota, he finds multiple upgrades he did not have in Arizona. For example, Murray has a star wideout for the first time since DeAndre Hopkins. Justin Jefferson is one of the best pass-catchers in the game, and just became the third player to ever begin a career with six straight seasons of 1,000 yards receiving. He's not the only weapon either, as Minnesota has a solid supporting cast which includes Aaron Jones, Jordan Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson and Jauan Jennings.
Murray also has the backing of a Brian Flores unit that finished No. 3 in total defense last season (282.6 yards allowed per game) and No. 7 in scoring defense (19.6 points allowed per game). If Murray can be an efficient distributor of the football, this Vikings team can return to the postseason. Why now, and what happens next?It's curious that the Vikings made this decision before the team's first preseason game, and that O'Connell didn't want to give his two quarterbacks a chance to compete with live reps. Sometimes it's the preseason where quarterback battles are decided, and now the NFL world is left with just one legitimate quarterback battle to follow this month with the Cleveland Browns. Tua Tagovailoa may have the Atlanta Falcons job wrapped up since Michael Penix Jr. hasn't even been cleared for 11-on-11 work.Ian Rapoport of NFL Network/ESPN said on "The Pat McAfee Show" that Murray and McCarthy pushed each other during this competition, but it did feel like the veteran was ahead. While the timing of this decision is surprising, what it does is give Minnesota's offense clarity, and the opportunity to practice full time with the new starting quarterback. No need to give McCarthy reps with the starting offense anymore. 
In an ironic twist of fate, the Vikings are hoping Murray can be their "Sam Darnold." Minnesota of course allowed Darnold to walk in free agency last offseason, and he was picked up by the Seattle Seahawks. Not many believed the journeyman could replicate a 14-3 season, but that's exactly what Darnold did as he helped Seattle not only win the NFC West and secure the No. 1 seed in the conference, but get over the hump entirely and win a Super Bowl.There are some obvious differences between Darnold and Murray. One was coming off the best season of his NFL career while the other is coming off arguably his worst. But O'Connell just needs someone to come in and run his system efficiently -- not be Superman. Reports from camp didn't indicate Murray was lighting up the practice field, and something to watch over the next month is how he adapts to O'Connell's timing-based passing attack. It's a bit different from what Murray has run in the past, and he needs to stay on time and in rhythm for it to work. Now that the competition has been decided, he has time to settle in.

title: Former All-Pro explains why he doesn't think Ben Roethlisberger is a Hall of Famer - CBS Sports
description: The former Steelers great will be eligible for the first time in 2027
body:
The former Steelers great will be eligible for the first time in 2027
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 11, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Conversations have already begun as it relates to the 2027 Pro Football Hall of Fame class and the insane number of notable players who will be eligible for the first time. Among those players is former quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, whose career includes two Super Bowl wins, 64,088 passing yards and 418 touchdowns and the fifth-most wins in NFL history among starting quarterbacks. While Roethlisberger's status as a first-ballot Hall of Famer is apparently up for debate, there is usually no arguing the fact that the Pittsburgh Steelers' former quarterback is undoubtedly a future Hall of Famer. However, LeSean McCoy, a former All-Pro running back, doesn't think that Roethlisberger had a Hall of Fame career based on his lack of individual accolades. "You should never be in the Hall of Fame if you never had no All-Pros," McCoy said on his podcast. "Think of how that sounds. All-Pro, for the guys that don't play football. All-Pro is the best in the league. You feel me? But I'm being serious, how the hell he not have (an) All-Pro? So, take him off."McCoy didn't change his opinion when it was pointed out to him that Roethlisberger likely would have garnered more individual honors had he played in a different era that didn't include Tom Brady, Peyton Manning, Aaron Rodgers and Drew Brees. 
"For me, I can't push your Hall of Fame with the best players of all time if you never had an All-Pro," he said. "Think about that though. That mean you never was the best quarterback or never was the best player in your position ever."  Roethlisberger's lack of individual accolades will likely be discussed when his candidacy is debated by the voters. And while McCoy doesn't agree, it won't keep Roethlisberger out of the Hall of Fame altogether. Roethlisberger's individual numbers -- that include his impressive wins total -- are just too good for him not to earn induction at some point if he is not inducted in 2027. The third quarterback taken in the 2004 NFL Draft (behind Eli Manning and Philip Rivers), Roethlisberger enjoyed one of the most successful rookie seasons in NFL history. He won his first 12 starts (an NFL record) en route to winning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year. 
The following season, Roethlisberger became the youngest starting quarterback to win the Super Bowl after helping the Steelers become the first sixth seed to win it all. His game-saving tackle in Pittsburgh's divisional round playoff win over the Colts kept the Steelers' championship run alive. Three years later, Roethlisberger engineered one of the most famous game-winning drives in NFL history that culminated in his game-winning touchdown pass to Santonio Holmes at the end of Super Bowl XLIII. 
Two years later, Roethlisberger again helped led the Steelers to the Super Bowl, where they were defeated by Rodgers and the Green Bay Packers. And while they did not get back to another Super Bowl after that, Steelers continued to be a perennial contender for the majority following decade largely because of Roethlisberger. 
Roethlisberger also accumulated some big numbers over that span that included becoming the first player to throw six touchdowns in consecutive games (doing so in 2014). He also owns the NFL record for most 500-yard passing performances (four). From 2014-18, Roethlisberger won a pair of passing titles and was named to four Pro Bowls. He also led the NFL in average passing yards per game on three occasions over that span. 
In addition to his numbers, Roethlisberger's reputation as one of the toughest quarterbacks in NFL history to bring down also strengthens his Hall of Fame argument. 
While he isn't sold on Roethlisberger, McCoy, thinks that one of Roethlisberger's former teammates, Antonio Brown, is not only of being inducted in his first year of eligibility, but he also believes that Brown was better than Jerry Rice, who is considered the greatest receiver of all time. Like Roethlisberger, Brown will be eligible for induction for the first time in 2027. "What can Jerry Rice do that AB can't do?" McCoy said. "I'm just saying, if AB played as long as (Rice) did, he would have more yards than him."
